topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and states what students should learn.

topics.label: Mutation accumulation and the development of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations give rise to cancer through clonal evolution shaped by cellular context and predisposition.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer risk and how evidence for that contribution is interpreted.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example of interacting infectious causes.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage capable of generating cancer-associated mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-initiating activity from the promotional conditions that allow mutated cells to proliferate.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility, with a recap of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete the explanation of context-dependent carcinogenesis by examining susceptibility at particular developmental stages and recapping the mechanisms already established.

topics.label: Evidence and methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence is obtained and interpreted to determine whether an exposure contributes to cancer.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and placing cancer risks in the context of everyday risk–benefit decisions.
